title: At 11, she broke a chess record that stood for two decades. October 1, 2026.
excerpt: From a government tourism company founded in 1966 to a reactor that makes its own fuel, October 1's five stories share one thread: none of them are overnight wins - every one of them is decades of unglamorous groundwork finally paying off.
bodyHtml:
Every story today is about groundwork that took years, sometimes decades, before it showed up as a headline - a tourism institution built brick by brick since 1966, a reactor design refined over decades of nuclear research, a raga tradition centuries old reaching a Grammy stage, a chess habit started during a pandemic breaking a 24-year-old record, and a scientist's journey from a village with no electricity to leading a national academy.

October 1, 1966: India decided tourism was worth its own government company

The India Tourism Development Corporation was incorporated on October 1, 1966, formed by merging several public-sector tourism bodies into one organization. It went on to operate the Ashok Group of Hotels, India's flagship government hospitality brand, along with duty-free retail and convention infrastructure including Pragati Maidan - the venue behind decades of India's biggest trade fairs.

At 11 years old, she just broke a chess record that stood for over two decades

Bodhana Sivanandan became the youngest Woman Grandmaster in chess history, at age 11, playing top board for England at the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. She broke a record held jointly by Kateryna Lagno and future Women's World Champion Hou Yifan, both of whom earned the title at age 12. She took up chess as a hobby during the COVID-19 pandemic.

She fuses Indian ragas with jazz. In 2026, that earned her a Grammy nomination

Charu Suri, born in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, earned a 2026 Grammy nomination for Best Contemporary Instrumental Album for her album 'Shayan', which blends Indian ragas with a jazz trio format. She's widely reported as the first raga-jazz artist ever nominated for a Grammy. She studied at Princeton and earned a Master's in Music from the Manhattan School of Music.

India just switched on a reactor that makes more fuel than it burns

On April 6, 2026, India's Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor at Kalpakkam, Tamil Nadu, attained first criticality - becoming the country's first operational fast breeder reactor, with a 500 MWe capacity. Designed by DAE's Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research, it uses indigenously produced Uranium-Plutonium fuel with a Uranium-238 blanket that breeds new fuel as it runs.

His village had no electricity until he was seven. He now leads Australia's national academy of science

Chennupati Jagadish grew up in the farming village of Vallurupalem, Andhra Pradesh, where his village had no electricity until he was about seven and he studied at night by kerosene lamp, walking roughly 5 kilometers barefoot each day to school. He moved to Australia in 1990, became a Distinguished Professor at the Australian National University, and in 2022 was elected President of the Australian Academy of Science - the first person of Indian origin to hold the role.

Five stories, one thread: a tourism institution that took decades to become the backbone it is today, a chess record that took a pandemic hobby and years of quiet practice to break, a jazz-raga sound that took centuries of tradition to reach a Grammy stage, a reactor that took decades of nuclear research to switch on, and a scientist whose journey from a village with no electricity to a national academy took a lifetime of persistence. Nothing here happened overnight. Everything here was overdue.
